summary: git stash sets uncommitted changes aside so you can switch tasks with a clean folder, then brings them back later.
notes: -m gives the stash a name you can read in git stash list.
git stash pop applies the newest stash and deletes it. git stash apply applies it and keeps it in the list.
Stashes are local. They are not pushed and they are easy to forget, so pop them soon.
pitfall: git stash skips untracked (new) files, so a new file stays in the folder. Use git stash -u to include them.
setup_note: Starts in a repository with two commits on main. README.md has a typo.
setup:
cat > gradebook.py <<'EOF'
scores = [88, 92, 79, 95]
average = sum(scores) / len(scores)
print("Average:", average)
EOF

cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# Gradebook
Quiz socres for Period 3.
EOF
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Add gradebook script"

cat > scores.csv <<'EOF'
name,score
Ava,88
Liam,92
Noah,79
Zoe,95
EOF
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Add quiz scores"
